en: The summary verse for the three topics is as follows:
Salutation, the number sixty, impurity, and through exhortations;
the unrighteous one, the Śākya, the sick person, and through quarreling.
The Chapter on Those Undergoing Probation;
the summary verse for the Chapter on Those Undergoing Probation:
Salutation, walking, seats, and families.
One should not dwell under the same roof, nor should one ordain [another] there;
one should not even go to a residence that has no monks, nor to a lower region where all gains are concentrated.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s monastery.
While lacking dispassion, monks committed an offense entailing suspension (saṃghāvaśeṣa).
Having become remorseful, they reflected:

How can we, being guilty of an offense, possessed of remorse, agitated, having further duties to perform, acting with brokenness, acting with speckled conduct, and acting with defilement— without having emerged from the root of the offense— accept from the monks who abide in their natural state the acts of salutation, veneration, rising to greet, joining the palms, and respectful conduct?
"We shall enjoy the first seat, the first water-offering, and the first portion of alms-food from faithful brahmin householders;

for the sake of a brief pleasure, we enter upon long-lasting suffering, wandering through the realms of hell-beings, animals, and hungry ghosts. What if we were to renounce the training and return to the lower life? And so, they renounce the training and return to the lower life.

They deceive those people who long for the going forth, saying, "Sirs, the holy life is difficult to practice; enough with the going forth. Because they themselves do not go forth and do not cause others to go forth, the number of monks has become small.
The community of monks has fallen into decline; it has become perforated and thinned out.
Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, being knowers and inquirers, ask; the Buddha, the Blessed One, asked the Venerable Ānanda.

"Ānanda, what is the cause, what is the condition, by which the monks have now become so few, and the community of monks has reached exhaustion, become riven, and become thin? He then reported this matter in detail to the Blessed One.
Then this occurred to the Blessed One:
"What if I were to grant a 'lifting of the hand' to those monks who have fallen into a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense, as a favor by means of this?
Having understood this, he assembled the community of monks and sat down on the seat prepared for him in front of the community of monks.
Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the monks:

"Monks, I have heard that you have fallen into an offense involving a formal meeting of the Saṃgha (saṃghāvaśeṣa), and having become remorseful, you have rejected the training and turned back toward decline.

Therefore, for the sake of the stability of the teaching and out of compassion for them, you must grant to those monks who have fallen into an offense involving a formal meeting of the Saṃgha the probation (parivāsa), the reduction of the root (mūlāpakarṣa), the penance (mānāpya), and the penance for the root (mūlamānāpya)."
He is to be suspended and granted a *mūlāpakarṣamānāpya*.
Furthermore, it should be granted in this manner:

having prepared the seating and bedding, having struck the gong, and having questioned the monks by means of a formal inquiry, when the entire Saṃgha is seated and assembled, [the procedure] should be performed by the most junior monk [concerning] the *parivāsa*...
It should be granted by a group of four belonging to the circle of the fourfold assembly.

A monk who has committed a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense, having performed the proper salutation according to seniority, should stand in a squatting position at the end of the row of elders and, with palms joined, request the *parivāsa*.
Furthermore, it should be requested in this manner:
"May the venerable Saṃgha listen.
I, the bhikṣu named so-and-so, have committed numerous *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offenses arising from intentional emission of semen, which were concealed for half a month.

I, the bhikṣu named so-and-so, [request] from the Saṃgha a half-month [parivāsa] for those numerous *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offenses arising from intentional emission of semen, which were concealed for half a month."

I request probation (*parivāsa*). May the venerable Saṃgha grant me, a monk of such-and-such a name, probation for one half-month for these numerous *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offenses arising from intentional emission of semen, which have been concealed for half a month.
Out of compassion, out of compassion, [the Sangha] grants him the parivāsa;
thus a second and a third time.
Thereafter, one monk, having made a formal motion (jñapti), should perform the ritual act (karman).
"Let the venerable Saṃgha listen.
This monk, named so-and-so, has committed numerous saṃghāvaśeṣa offenses arising from intentional emission of semen, which were concealed for half a month."
This monk, [named] so-and-so, requests from the Saṃgha a half-month’s parivāsa for these many saṃghāvaśeṣa offenses arising from intentional emission of semen, which were concealed for half a month.
If it seems the proper time to the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha, if it approves, grant that the Saṃgha [grant] a half-month’s parivāsa to the monk [named] so-and-so.
For these numerous saṃghāvaśeṣa offenses arising from intentional emission of semen and concealed for half a month,
one should grant a half-month parivāsa. This is the motion (jñapti).
The formal act (*karma*) should be performed:
Listen, venerable Saṃgha!
This monk, named so-and-so, has committed numerous *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offenses arising from intentional emission of semen, which were concealed for half a month.

This monk, named so-and-so, requests from the Saṃgha a half-month’s *parivāsa* for these many *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offenses arising from intentional emission of semen, which have been concealed for half a month. Therefore, the Saṃgha grants a half-month’s *parivāsa* to this monk, named so-and-so, for these many *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offenses arising from intentional emission of semen.
If it is pleasing to these venerable ones to grant a half-month *parivāsa* for these many *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offenses of the monk named so-and-so—
offenses arising from intentional emission of semen and concealed for half a month— they should remain silent;
those who do not approve should speak.
This first formal proclamation (karmavācanā) should be uttered:
"The Saṃgha has granted a half-month’s parivāsa for these many saṃghāvaśeṣa offenses of the monk named so-and-so,
which arose from intentional emission of semen and were concealed for half a month."
"It has been endured and permitted by the Saṃgha, since there is silence; thus do I hold it to be so. It was said by the Blessed One:
"Parivāsa and mūlaparivāsa are to be granted," and so forth.

The group-of-six monks, while undergoing the period of probation and the *mānāpya* penance, accepted from the regular (*prakṛtistha*) monks greetings, salutations, rising to meet them, joining their palms, and acts of respectful courtesy.

The monks of little purpose reproached, reviled, and censured this, saying: "This is neither clever nor fitting, that these monks undergoing probation and the *mānāpya* penance now accept from the regular monks greetings, salutations, rising to meet them, joining their palms, and acts of respectful courtesy."
The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
"Monks, I shall prescribe the rules of proper conduct for monks who are undergoing the *pārivāsa* and *mānāpya* penances."

Monks who are undergoing the *pārivāsa* or *mānāpya* penances must not accept from regular (*prakṛtistha*) monks the acts of salutation, prostration, rising to greet, joining the palms, or respectful homage.
They must not sit on the same seat,
nor even on a seat that is equal in height.
If they sit down, one should sit having taken a lower seat.
One should not walk up and down the path at the same time as them,
nor ahead of them.
If they walk the walking-path, they should do so with a reduction in their steps.
They should not approach brahmin families;
if they do approach them, it must be in the manner of a junior monk.
One should not dwell under one roof;
one should not grant the going-forth;
one should not confer full ordination.
No formal reliance (niśraya) should be granted; no novice (śramaṇoddeśī) should be ordained;
and no formal act (karman) should be performed.
One should not be appointed as a karma-kāraka;
one should not instruct the bhikṣuṇīs;
nor should one be appointed as an instructor of bhikṣuṇīs.
Nuns must not be instructed by one who has not previously been authorized.
Nor should a monk be reproached,
reminded, or censured on account of a failure in morality, a failure in view, a failure in conduct, or a failure in livelihood.
One should not, by means of this, establish formal instruction;

nor the Poṣadha ceremony, nor the Pravāraṇā, nor a motion (jñapti), nor a motion followed by one proclamation (jñaptidvitīya), nor a formal act followed by three proclamations (jñapticaturtha). Having risen early in the morning, the door should be opened.
The lamp-stand should be wiped clean; the monastery should be sprinkled with water and swept.
A tender layer of cow dung should be applied;
the latrines and urinals should be cleaned;
clay should be kept ready, as well as bowls and cool water, in accordance with the season.
The openings of the conduits must be cleaned.
Having recognized the proper time, one should arrange the seating and place incense in the incense burner.
If one is capable, one should personally perform the proclamation of the Teacher’s virtues.
Otherwise, the reciter should be questioned. Having inspected the supplementary food offerings, if they have been brought, he should ascend to the roof of the shelter and strike the gong.
During the summer season, he should take a fan for the monks.
Then, having placed himself behind all those who are fully ordained, maintaining a calm deportment, he should eat while attending upon the community of monks.
Having finished the meal, the bedding and seats should be protected by covering them;
the bowl-stand should be discarded. Knowing the proper time, the stūpas of the Tathāgata’s hair and nails should be swept and a fine coating of cow dung should be applied.
Furthermore, at the time of the assembly, the preparation of the bedding and seats must be made;
incense should be placed in the incense burner;
and the proclamation of the Teacher’s qualities must be performed as before.
The day must be announced:
"May the venerable Saṃgha listen;
today is the tenth day of the fortnight," and so forth, just as the officers in charge of the requisites announce it.
Then the *parivāsa* (probation) must be announced:
"Listen, venerable Saṃgha!
I, the monk named so-and-so, have committed such and such a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense, which was concealed for this length of time."
"The Saṃgha has granted me a period of parivāsa for such a length of time.
Therefore, I have practiced this much, and the remainder must still be practiced.
May the venerable Saṃgha recognize me as one who is undergoing parivāsa and as one who is practicing mānāpya."
The Blessed One has said,
"The *parivāsa* must be announced," yet he does not announce it to those who have arrived.
The Blessed One said,
"It should be announced to the guests.
Thus it was spoken by the Blessed One.
"It should also be announced to those who have arrived as guests.
Now, a certain guest monk arrived;
before he had even set down his bowl and robe, the one undergoing probation stood before him and said:
Pay attention to me, venerable sir:
I, a monk named so-and-so, have committed an offense entailing suspension (*saṃghāvaśeṣa*). [As before,] may the venerable one maintain me as one undergoing the period of probation (*pārivāsika*).
Standing before him, he said, "Get away from me, you deluded man! Do not stay here; do not be near me!
With his heart overwhelmed by shame, his face cast downward, he departed from the presence of that monk with a slow and faltering gait.
The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
"When a visiting monk has not yet been assigned a bowl and robe, one must not inform him [of the offense]."
"However, it should not be announced to each individual; rather, it should be done when the entire Saṃgha is seated together in assembly.
The Blessed One said:
When the gaṇḍī has been struck, he should announce it to those who are present.
He must not go to a monastery that is devoid of monks;
if he goes there, he must not reside there.
At the improper time, the feet of the monks should be washed with warm water or cold water as appropriate for the time,
and they should be anointed;
unless they do not wish it.
The withdrawal of affection and gain must be performed.
Then, having established mindfulness, one should prepare for sleep while maintaining the perception of rising.
This applies to those undergoing the *pārivāsa* and *mānāpya* penances.
If monks do not undertake and abide by the rules of customary conduct as they have been prescribed, they become guilty of an offense; [the community] does not assign them a dwelling,
nor does it provide them with gains.
The Blessed One said:
"His dwelling should be assigned last of all,
and his share of the acquisitions should be given last of all."
The summary verse:
One should perform one hundred and sixty [days]; and indeed, from the group of twenty;
the *mānāpya* should be practiced in the Saṃgha; those who have returned are the obstructors.
The group of six monks, while themselves undergoing the probationary period (*pārivāsika*) and the penance (*mānāpyacārika*), granted probation to other monks.
The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
The probation (pārivāsa) of a monk should not be granted by four monks who are themselves on probation; nor by three monks on probation and one who is in his natural state (prakṛtistha);
nor by two monks on probation and two who are in their natural state.

The probation (*parivāsa*) of a monk must not be granted by one who is himself on probation, nor by three who are in their natural state; rather, it must be granted by all who are pure and hold the same view.

Just as it is with those on probation, so it is with those on initial probation (*mūlaparivāsa*), those practicing the penance of reconciliation (*mānāpyacārika*), and those who have completed that penance (*caritamānāpya*).
Just as it is with *parivāsa*, so it is with *mūlaparivāsa*, *mūlāpakarṣa*, *mānāpya*, *mūlamānāpya*, and *mūlāpakarṣamānāpya*.
The monks of the group of six, while themselves undergoing *parivāsa* and practicing *mānāpya*, performed the *āvarhaṇa* (rehabilitation) of other monks.
The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
"A monk should not be reintegrated by twenty *pārivāsika* monks;
nor should he be reintegrated by nineteen *pārivāsika* monks together with one *prakṛtisthaka*."
It is not [valid] with eighteen *pārivāsika* monks and two *prakṛtisthaka* monks, and so on, up to nineteen *prakṛtisthaka* monks and one *pārivāsika* monk.

As it is with the *pārivāsikas*, so it is with those who have completed their *parivāsa* (*paryuṣitaparivāsa*), those undergoing *mānāpya*, those who have completed their *mānāpya* (*cāritamānāpya*), and those granted training (*śikṣādattaka*).
The group-of-six monks, being themselves *pārivāsika-mānāpyacārika*, performed their *parivāsa* in the presence of monks who were *pārivāsika*.
The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
"A monk must not undergo the probationary period (parivāsa) in the presence of four [other] monks who are themselves undergoing probation."
It is not [permissible] for three who are undergoing probation (pārivāsika) with one who is in his original state (prakṛtisthaka);
nor for two who are undergoing probation with two who are in their original state;
nor for three who are in their original state with one who is undergoing probation.
Rather, the *parivāsa* must be undergone in the presence of all those who are pure and hold the same view.

As it is for those undergoing *parivāsa*, so it is for those who have completed their *parivāsa*, for those practicing *mānāpya*, for those who have completed their *mānāpya*, and for those to whom a *śikṣādattaka* penance has been assigned.
Just as it is with *parivāsa*, so it is with *mūlaparivāsa*, *mūlāpakarṣa*, *mānāpya*, *mūlamānāpya*, and *mūlāpakarṣamānāpya*.
The group-of-six monks, being in the state of those undergoing probation (*pārivāsika*) and penance (*mānāpyacārika*), went to an empty monastery and performed their probation there.
They were seen by other monks and addressed:
"Venerable ones, has this monastery been occupied by you?"
They said,
"This has not been inhabited by us;
rather, we are undergoing the parivāsa penance."
They said:
"You should undergo the *parivāsa* penance;
why then do you conceal [your offenses]?"
Struck by them, they remained silent.
The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
“Monks, the *parivāsa* penance is not to be undergone in an empty dwelling, nor where there is only one, two, or three monks;
rather, it is to be undergone where four monks who are pure and of identical view reside.”
(311v1 = GBM 6.935) Just as it is with *parivāsa*, so it is with *mūlaparivāsa*, *mūlāpakarṣa*, *mānāpya*, *mūlamānāpya*, and *mūlāpakarṣamānāpya*.
Then the Venerable Upāli questioned the Buddha, the Blessed One:

"Furthermore, venerable sir, it has been heard by those undergoing probation (*pārivāsika*) and penance (*mānāpyacārika*): 'Monks who are makers of strife, makers of quarrels, makers of disputes, makers of contention, and creators of legal issues are coming; they will reproach us either shamelessly or with contempt.
How, then, should they conduct themselves toward them?"
The Blessed One said:
"Upāli, when monks who are undergoing probation or the *mānāpya* penance hear that quarrelsome monks are approaching, they must relinquish that probation in the presence of those monks.
And it should be relinquished in this manner:"
Having arranged his robes properly, standing in a squatting posture and raising his joined palms, he should speak as follows:
"Pay attention, Venerable One! I, named so-and-so, have committed such and such a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense, which was concealed for this length of time.
For that offense, the Saṃgha has granted me *parivāsa* for this length of time."

While I was a *pārivāsika*, I heard that monks who are quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, argumentative, and litigious were coming; they might reproach me or remind me of my offense, either shamelessly or with malice.
Therefore, I, the monk named so-and-so, being a *pārivāsika*, relinquish that *parivāsa* before the Venerable One.
"For so long has this been my conduct, and for so long must it still be practiced;
may the Venerable One regard me as one established in his natural state."

Then, once again, when their momentum has passed, their impetuosity has been spent, and they are free from adversaries, the *parivāsa* should be undertaken in the presence of a monk who is in his natural state (*prakṛtisthaka*).
And it should be undertaken in this manner:
having arranged oneself properly, standing in a squatting position (*utkuṭuka*) with palms joined in reverence (*añjali*), this should be said:
"Pay attention, Venerable One! I, the monk named so-and-so, have committed such and such a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense, concealed for this long a period of time.
The Saṃgha has granted me *parivāsa* for that duration.
While I was undergoing that *parivāsa*, I heard that monks who are quarrelsome, contentious, and argumentative are coming."
Those who cause disputes and handle legal cases might reproach me or remind me of my offense out of shamelessness or for the sake of a reward.
Therefore, I have relinquished the conduct of one undergoing *pārivāsa* before a monk.
I, the monk named [so-and-so], now formally undertake that period of *parivāsa* in the presence of the Venerable One.
"For this much time I have practiced [the penance], and for this much time my duty will remain to be performed.
Venerable sir, please recognize me as one who is undergoing *parivāsa*.
As it is with *parivāsa*, so it is with *mūlaparivāsa*, *mūlāpakarṣa*, and *mānāpya*."
The section on those undergoing probation is concluded.
